Live from NPR News in New York City, I'm Dua Elisa Kautau. The White House has signed an order that temporarily halts new sanctions against Russia.
The move comes just days before the sanctions were to take effect, as NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
The sanctions were part of a package of financial measures designed to put pressure on Russia and named after the late Senator, Lindsey Graham, who led the effort.
Trump, who signed the legislation last month, put a hold on the implementation, arguing that the pause was in the national interest.
It follows another controversial announcement Trump made, that the U.S. would be purchasing diesel fuel from Russia.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky criticized the decision, charging that the U.S. is easing pressure on Russia, just as Russia carries out massive attacks on Ukraine's energy sector.
Zelensky wrote on social media that the Graham-led sanctions would have helped enormously, and that more pressure is needed on Russia instead of financial rewards.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
The group No Kings is trying to activate early voting across the country this weekend.
Brooke Thorrington with member station WRKF is in Baton Rouge.
Even though the sprinklers were at full blast on the capital grounds, it didn't deter the crowd.
Quentin Anderson with the Bayou Progressive led the call to action.
Right now is the most important moment in history because right now we can still impact the outcome.
We can't complain after the fact if we don't show up on November 3rd.
Two Democratic candidates running in the Stage 6 congressional district also attended.
That's the district at the center of the U.S. Supreme Court ruling.
It prompted southern red states to redraw their maps to help Republicans.
Even though the district favors the GOP now, three Democrats, six Republicans, and a Libertarian are on the ballot for the congressional open primary.
For NPR News, I'm Brooke Thorrington.
Immigrants in a southeast Georgia ICE detention facility are on a hunger strike protesting what they say are prolonged detentions in subpar conditions.
From member station WAB in Atlanta, Emily Wu-Pearson reports.
The hunger strike started October 6th.
It comes after 45 men held in the Folkston D. Ray James ICE processing center published a letter explaining many of them are asylum seekers from countries like Russia, China, Afghanistan, and Nepal.
Many have been detained for years, some since the Biden administration.
They allege insufficient medical care, food that makes people sick, and dirty facilities.
ICE says it's monitoring the situation and will "intervene when it becomes necessary."
There have been hunger strikes at ICE facilities over the years, not just during the Trump administration's.
And strikers have been force fed in the past.
For NPR News, I'm Emily Wu-Pearson in Atlanta.
And you're listening to NPR from New York City.
A new report by the Vatican says the number of Catholics in Africa has surpassed Europe for the first time ever.
Officials say Africa also recorded the highest worldwide increase in the number of Catholics, and it appears Jewell Bright reports.
The report by the Vatican's Fidesz News Agency says Africa's Catholic population grew by over 7 million to 288 million by June 2024, slightly ahead of Europe's 287 million.
Globally, the Catholic Church's population stands at 1.4 billion, representing around 17% of the global population.
The Americas remain home to the largest population of Catholics globally, with over 600 million faithful.
The report also recorded a slight increase in the number of priests worldwide.
But there was a decline in the number of Catholic women's religious groups and major seminarians.
Jewell Bright, NPR News, Vegas.
Pope Leo smiled gently as he walked out of a Rome hospital this afternoon,
unassisted and waving to a crowd that applauded as he stepped into a black SUV to return home to the Vatican.
He's been recovering from getting a tumor removed from his right lung.
The 71-year-old was diagnosed recently with adenocarcinoma, a common type of lung cancer found in non-smokers.
Officials at the Vatican say the Pope is not receiving private audiences at the moment,
but he plans to deliver his weekly prayer on Sunday.
The Holy Father is still scheduled to visit ten cities in Latin America in November.
I'm Dua Lisa Kautel, NPR News in New York.
